questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms is associated with Hindustani Classical Music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Kathak.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India and originated in North India.**
 
• The dance form has its roots in the Mughal era and is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful hand movements, and storytelling through facial expressions.
 
• Kathak is closely associated with Hindustani classical music and is often performed to the accompaniment of tabla, sarangi, and sitar.
 
• The nineteenth century saw the **golden age of Kathak under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah, the last Nawab of Oudh.**
 
• He established the **Lucknow Gharana with its strong accent on bhava, the expression of moods and emotions.**
 
• The **Jaipur Gharana is known for its layakari or rhythmic virtuosity and the Benaras Gharana is another prominent school of Kathak dance**.
 
• The technique of movement in Kathak is unique.
 
• Today, Kathak has **emerged as a distinct dance form**.
 
• Being the only classical dance of India having links with Muslim culture, it represents a unique synthesis of Hindu and Muslim genius in art.
 
• **Further, Kathak is the only form of classical dance wedded to Hindustani or North Indian music.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​__Kathak dance is a combination of music, dance, and narrative. 
 
• The name Kathak is derived from the Sanskrit word *katha* meaning story.
 
• This dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathaks, or storytellers.
 
• The present-day Kathak dance mainly depends on the medieval period *Ras Lila*, a local dance in the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an NGO involved in microfinance-related activities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD in Mumbai.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **NGO stands for Non-Governmental Organization,** which is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. NGOs are usually involved in social, cultural, and environmental activities to promote social welfare.
 
• **Microfinance is a financial service **provided to low-income individuals or groups who do not have access to traditional banking services. Microfinance institutions provide small loans, savings, insurance, and other financial services to help people improve their livelihoods.
 
• **MYRADA in Bangalore is an NGO** that works in the areas of rural development, natural resource management, and microfinance. SEWA in Ahmedabad is another NGO that provides microfinance services to women entrepreneurs. ADITHI in Patna is an NGO that works for the empowerment of women and children through education, health, and livelihood programs.
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) **is a development bank that provides financial and technical assistance to rural areas in India. While NABARD supports microfinance institutions and self-help groups, it is not an NGO as it is a government-owned institution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A large amount of loan is not a basic principle of micro-financial institutions in India.
 
• The functions of Microfinance institutions are:
 
 
• Maintain macroeconomic stability.
 
• Avoid interest-rate caps.
 
• Refrain from distorting the market with unsustainable subsidized.
 
• High-delinquency loan programs.
 
 
 
• MFIs are financial companies that provide small loans to people who do not have any access to banking facilities.
 
• The definition of “small loans” varies between countries. In India, all loans that are below Rs. 1 lakh can be considered as microloans.
 
• Various types of institutions offer microfinance:
 
 
• ​Credit unions.
 
• Commercial banks.
 
• NGOs (Non-governmental Organizations).
 
• Cooperatives, and sectors of government banks.
 
 
 
• The emergence of “for-profit” MFIs is growing. In India, these 'for-profit' MFIs are referred to as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFC).

questions.question: Which of the following committees had recommended to incorporate the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Swaran Singh Committee.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution through the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• At present, there are eleven fundamental duties under Article 51 A of the Constitution.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties has been borrowed from the erstwhile USSR.
 
• Originally the duties were ten in number, later on through the 86th Amendment Act, of 2002, the eleventh Fundamental duty was added.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-enforceable in nature.
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **The Sarkaria Commission was set up on 9th June 1983 by the Government of India.**

 
 
• Aim: To review the relations between the Centre and the States.
 
• Justice Rajendra Singh Sarkaria, a retired Judge of SC of India, was the Chairman of the commission.
 
• The other two members of the commission were:
 
 
• Shri B. Sivaraman
 
• Dr S R Sen​
 
 
 
 
 
• **PB Patil Committee was constituted for the evaluation of the Panchayat Raj system in 1984.**
 
 
• The committee emphasized involving people and gave 184 recommendations for reforming the system and enabling greater participation.
 
 
 
• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed to examine the working of the community development program and the national extension service.
 
 
• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was appointed in 1957.
 
• Balwant Rai Mehta was the chairman of this committee.
 
• **The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee recommended establishing a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure.**

• ** Pratham Bank was established in 1975 as the first Regional Rural Bank of India.**
 
• Its Head Office was located in** Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding liquidity trap?

i. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely inelastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

ii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly inelastic.

iii. It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.

iv. It is the point where speculative demand for money and the liquidity preference curves are not related.

options.text: Only Statements i and ii are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement iii is correct.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A liquidity trap is a situation where monetary policy becomes ineffective due to the zero lower bound on interest rates.**
 
• **​**Liquidity trap:
 
• A liquidity trap refers to a situation in which an increase in the money supply does not result in a fall in the interest rate but merely in addition to idle balances the interest elasticity of demand for money becomes infinite.
 
• Under normal conditions, an increase in money supply, resulting in excess cash balances, would cause an increase in bond prices, as individuals sought to acquire assets in exchange for money, and a corresponding fall in interest rates.
 
• The horizontal portion of the liquidity preference curve is referred to as the liquidity trap.
 
• In this portion of the curve, the demand for money is infinitely elastic with respect to the interest rate.
 
• Re­ductions in the interest rate, in this portion only, increase people’s desire to hold cash balances
 
• Statement 3 is correct as It is the point where speculative demand for money is infinitely elastic and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly elastic.
 
• In a liquidity trap, people prefer holding money regardless of the interest rate because they expect that the return on other assets will not be better. Therefore, the demand for money is infinitely elastic (it does not change with interest rates), and the liquidity preference curve becomes perfectly horizontal or elastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__"**

 
• 
 
Speculative Demand for Money: In a liquidity trap, speculative demand for money is actually infinitely elastic, not inelastic. This means that people are willing to hold an unlimited amount of money at a particular low interest rate, because they expect interest rates to rise in the future, which would cause bond prices to fall.

 
 
• 
 
Liquidity Preference Curve: The curve becomes perfectly elastic (horizontal) at the liquidity trap, indicating that changes in the money supply will not affect interest rates because people prefer to hold money rather than invest in bonds.

 Thus, this statement is incorrect because it incorrectly describes speculative demand for money as infinitely inelastic

questions.question: Cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital is referred to as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**extensive cultivation.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Extensive cultivation refers to the practice of cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital. It is also known as extensive subsistence agriculture.**
 
• This type of cultivation is usually practiced in areas with low population density and abundant land resources.
 
• The main aim of extensive cultivation is to produce enough** food to meet the needs **of the family or community without the use of modern technology or intensive inputs.
 
• The crops grown in **extensive cultivation** are usually low-yielding and require less maintenance and care than in **intensive cultivation.**
 
• The other options are not correct because** hybrid cultivation** refers to the practice of growing genetically modified crops, intensive cultivation involves high inputs of labor and capital to produce high yields, and capitalist cultivation is a term used to** describe large-scale commercial farming done by corporations.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Hybrid cultivation** is a type of farming that involves the cross-breeding of two different plant varieties to create a new variety with desirable traits. This type of cultivation is often used to produce crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, have higher yields, and can tolerate harsh environmental conditions.
 
• ** Intensive cultivation** is a type of farming that involves high inputs of labor, capital, and technology to produce high yields of crops. This type of cultivation is often used in areas with high population density and limited land resources.
 
• **Capitalist cultivation** is a term used to describe the large-scale commercial farming done by corporations. This type of cultivation is often characterized by the use of modern technology, high inputs of labor and capital, and the production of crops for the global market.

questions.question: What was the percentage of women working in the primary sector of India as of 2011-2012?

__
 
• **The primary sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining. As of 2011-2012, the percentage of women working in the primary sector in India was 62.8 percent.**
 
• **Women's participation** in the workforce has been increasing in recent years, but there is still a significant gender gap.
 
• According to the World Bank, in 2019, the labor force participation rate for women in India was **22.3%, compared to 76.5% for men.**
 
• The primary sector is an important part of the Indian economy, accounting for around **16% of the country's GDP in 2020.**
 
• However, the sector is also facing challenges such as **low productivity, climate change, and rural-urban migration.**
 
• The government has implemented various policies and schemes to promote women's participation in the workforce, such as the **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) for women farmers and the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) for rural women.**
 
• In addition to the primary sector, women are also employed in other sectors such as manufacturing, services, and the informal sector.
 
• However, women's participation in these sectors is also lower than men's, and they often face discrimination and unequal pay.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee of 2021, Kanaka Raju is associated with which of the following tribal folk dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Gussadi.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points:__

__
 
• **Kanaka Raju**

questions.question: The hardness of water is expressed in terms of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ppm.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The hardness of water is the measure of the concentration of dissolved minerals, primarily calcium and magnesium ions, in water.**
 
• The most common unit of measuring water hardness is** parts per million (ppm).**
 
• Molarity is the measure of the concentration of a solution in terms of the number of moles of **solute per liter of solution.**
 
 
• It is not used to** express water hardness.**
 
 
 
• Normality is a measure of the concentration of a solution in terms of the number of equivalents of solute per liter of solution.
 
 
• It is also not used to express water hardness.
 
 
 
• A mole is the amount of a substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in 12 grams of carbon-12. It is not used to express water hardness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mole: **It is a unit of measurement used in chemistry to express amounts of a chemical substance. It is defined as the amount of a substance that contains the same number of particles as there are atoms in 12 grams of carbon-12.
 
• **Molarity:** It is a measure of the concentration of a solution in terms of the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is commonly used in chemistry to express the concentration of a solution.
 
• **Normality:** It is a measure of the concentration of a solution in terms of the number of equivalents of solute per liter of solution. It is commonly used in acid-base chemistry to express the concentration of an acid or a base.
 
• **Parts per million (ppm): **It is a unit of measurement used to express the concentration of a substance in a solution. It is defined as the number of parts of a substance per one million parts of the solution. It is commonly used to express the concentration of minerals in water.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common product offered by microfinance institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit cards.**__

__
 
• Microfinance institutions in India primarily focus on providing financial services to the **economically weaker sections of society **who do not have access to formal banking services.
 
• The most common products offered by microfinance institutions in India are **personal loans, insurance products, and savings accounts**. These products are designed to meet the specific financial needs of the target customers and are offered at affordable interest rates.
 
• **Credit cards are not typically offered by microfinance institutions in India. This is because credit cards are generally associated with higher credit risk and require a certain level of creditworthiness to qualify for them.**
 
• Personal loans are one of the most popular products offered by microfinance institutions in India.
 
 
• These loans are typically used for meeting various personal expenses such as medical emergencies, education, and home renovation.
 
 
 
• ** Insurance products** such as life insurance and health insurance are also commonly offered by microfinance institutions in India. These products provide financial protection to the customers and their families in case of unforeseen events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Personal loans**: These are** unsecured loans** that do not require any collateral. The loan amount is typically small, and the repayment tenure can range from a few months to a few years.
 
• **Insurance products: **Microfinance institutions in India offer various **insurance products such as life insurance, health insurance, and crop insurance.** These products are designed to provide financial protection to the customers and their families in case of unforeseen events.
 
• **Saving accounts**: These are basic savings accounts that can be opened with a small deposit. The interest rates offered on these accounts are usually higher than those offered by traditional banks.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted during the regime of which viceroy of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Vernacular Press Act 1878:**

__
 
• ​__British India passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to **restrict press freedom and discourage criticism of British policy,** notably the opposition that had risen since the commencement of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80).
 
• **The Act was submitted by Lytton, the Viceroy of India at the time, and on March 14, 1878, **the Viceroy's Council unanimously approved it. In order to "better control" the vernacular press and effectively penalize and prohibit "seditious literature" in "publications in oriental languages," the Vernacular Press Act (VPA) was passed.
 
• As a result, the British had nothing but hatred for the (non-English speaking) Indian press.
 
• It was also known as the Gagging Act.
 
• It was an act for the better control of publication in oriental languages.
 
• It was primarily targeted against Amrit Bazar Patrika.
 
• The act was repealed by Lord Ripon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856. He was known for his policies of annexation and modernization, including the Doctrine of Lapse and the construction of railways and telegraph lines.
 
• Lord Hastings was the Governor-General of India from 1813 to 1823. He was known for his military campaigns, including the Anglo-Nepalese War and the First Anglo-Burmese War.
 
• Lord Ripon was the Viceroy of India from 1880 to 1884. He was known for his liberal policies, including the repeal of the Vernacular Press Act and the introduction of local self-government.

questions.question: The photoelectric effect demonstrates which nature of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Particle nature.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Photoelectric effect:**

__
 
• **The phenomenon in which light energy forces a metal surface to release electrons is called the photoelectric effect.**
 
• When the light hits, it shows the particle theory of light, and light is defined as a stream of photons or energy packets.
 
• The other phenomena such as interference, diffraction, and polarization can only be explained when the light is treated as a wave wherein the photoelectric effect, **line spectra, and the production and scattering of x-rays demonstrate the particle nature of light.**

**Properties of Lightwaves:**

 
• Not have any charge or we can say that they are neutral.
 
• Propagate as a transverse wave with both wave and particle nature.
 
• **They move with a velocity the same as that of light i.e. 3 × 10⁸ m/s.**
 
• It contains energy and it also contains momentum.
 
• They can travel in a vacuum and always travel in a straight line.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Crystalline nature** refers to the regular, **repeating structure of a solid,** which can affect how light interacts with it.

 
 
• However, it is not directly related to the photoelectric effect.
 
 
 
• ** Wave nature refers** to the fact that light can exhibit interference and diffraction patterns, similar to water waves or sound waves.
 
 
• This is important in many areas of physics,** but again, not directly relevant to the photoelectric effect.**

questions.question: From which place did the Revolt of 1857 start?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meerut.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Revolt of 1857 was the first rebellion against the British East India Company.**
 
• The first war of Indian Independence started on 10th May 1857.
 
• **The revolt was started at Meerut.**
 
• It began as a revolt of the sepoys of the British East India Company’s army but eventually secured the participation of the masses.
 
• The issue of greased cartridges and military grievances has been over-emphasized as the factor for the Revolt of 1857.
 
• In March **1857, Mangal Pandey, a sepoy in Barrackpore, refused to use the cartridge and attacked his senior officers.**
 
• **He was hanged to death on 8th April 1857.**
 
• On 9th May 1857, 85 soldiers in Meerut refused to use the new rifle and were sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment.
 
• The revolt is known by several names: the Sepoy Mutiny (by the British Historians), the Indian Mutiny, the Great Rebellion (by the Indian Historians), the Revolt of 1857, the Indian Insurrection, and the First War of Independence (by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar).
 
• Lord Canning was the British viceroy during the revolt of 1857.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The main causes of revolt were the contemporary Religious & Social, Political, and Economic scenarios of the country. 
 
• The revolt is known by different names:
 
 
• The Sepoy Mutiny (by the British Historians)
 
• The Indian Mutiny 
 
• The Great Rebellion (by the Indian Historians)
 
• The Revolt of 1857
 
• The First War of Independence (by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra:** Agra was an important city during th**e Mughal era **and was the capital of the **Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. **
 
• **Kanpur**: Kanpur was one of the major centers of the revolt and was the site of the **infamous Bibighar massacre, where British women and children were killed by rebels**. However, it was not the starting point of the revolt.
 
• **Delhi: **Delhi was the center of the rebellion and the site of the formation of the **rebel government, with Bahadur Shah Zafar as the nominal leader.**
